claim: Hidden states of LLMs primarily encode whether the model is performing parametric knowledge recall, not whether the output is actually truthful -- so hallucinations driven by spurious learned associations (Associated Hallucinations) have hidden-state geometry that overlaps heavily with genuinely correct outputs and evade standard probe-based detectors.
stance_target: internal hidden-state probes are a clean, universal correctness/truthfulness detector
scope_conditions: General factual QA/hallucination benchmarks; whole-output granularity; taxonomy of Unassociated vs Associated Hallucinations
quoted_support: Our results show that hidden states primarily reflect whether the model is recalling parametric knowledge rather than the truthfulness of the output itself. Consequently, AHs exhibit hidden-state geometries that largely overlap with factual outputs, rendering standard detection methods ineffective.

claim: Unassociated Hallucinations (outputs lacking any parametric grounding) exhibit distinctive, clustered hidden-state representations that remain reliably detectable, unlike Associated Hallucinations.
stance_target: internal probes retain partial validity for a subset of hallucination types even though they are confounded for others
quoted_support: In contrast, UHs exhibit distinctive, clustered representations that facilitate reliable detection.
